newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips to launch rewritable CD in March.
newsitem.headline: Philips to launch rewritable CD in March.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Tuesday it would launch its recordable compact disc (CD) drive for data applications in Europe and the U.S. at next month's CeBIT electronics trade fair in Germany.
Philips is to introduce its CD Rewritable (CD-RW) drives for around $900 each, with CD-RW discs selling for around $25, said Jan Oosterveld, president of Philips Key Modules.
"Our estimates are that over the next two to three years more than 30 million CD-Rewritable discs will be sold," he told journalists at Philips' pre-CeBIT briefing.
Oosterveld said the discs could be used as giant computer floppy discs or large removable hard discs and were mainly intended for data interchange and personal archiving markets.
The technology involves heating and crystallising the CD's material during rewriting -- a process which can be repeated at least 1,000 times, he said.

He said the CD-ROM drive market was still showing steady growth. "We expect that 80 percent of all PCs to be sold in 1997 will be equipped with a CD-ROM drive. For home PCs, the attach rate is already 100 percent," said Oosterveld.

He said that in absolute figures, the read only memory (ROM) drive market would grow from a current 50 million a year now to close to 100 million by the end of the decade. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
